author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Australia’s government has proposed legislation that would require social-media platforms to let users age 16 and older opt out of algorithmically recommended feeds.

Under the plan, services would have to notify eligible users and provide a genuine, enduring choice between recommendation-driven content and a feed centered on friends or creators they follow. The proposal extends Australia’s scrutiny of platform design beyond its existing ban on social-media accounts for children under 16.

A broader digital duty of care would also apply to services including games, apps and artificial-intelligence chatbots. Those companies would be expected to protect children from features regulators consider addictive or damaging to self-esteem. The maximum penalty described for a breach is 109.2 million Australian dollars, equivalent to about $78.6 million in the Associated Press report.

The measures are proposed laws and have not yet taken effect. Their practical impact will depend on the final text, parliamentary approval and enforcement rules. If enacted, the opt-out requirement could test whether large platforms can provide a truly persistent non-algorithmic experience rather than a temporary setting that quietly resets.
dek: Draft legislation would require social platforms to give users 16 and older a lasting choice between recommended content and posts from accounts they follow.
headline: Australia proposes right to opt out of algorithmic feeds
